intent: TIT-004 follow-up: replace the organization-licensed proprietary gitleaks-action wrapper with the checksum-pinned MIT Gitleaks 8.30.1 CLI while preserving the required gitleaks check identity, adding explicit pull-request, push, merge-group, and manual-audit revision ranges, and reducing workflow authority to contents read.

negative_controls.name: checksum-pin-mutation-is-rejected
negative_controls.command: python3 -c "from pathlib import Path; t=Path('.github/workflows/gitleaks.yml').read_text(); d='551f6fc83ea457d62a0d98237cbad105af8d557003051f41f3e7ca7b3f2470eb'; m=t.replace(d,'0'*64,1); raise SystemExit(1 if d not in m else 0)"

commit.message: fix(ci): migrate gitleaks to pinned MIT CLI

interface_mismatches: The workflow declared merge_group support, but the pinned v2 wrapper rejects merge_group events before scanning; the replacement must derive and scan the merge-group base_sha..head_sha candidate explicitly.
The proprietary action requires GITLEAKS_LICENSE for organization-owned repositories, while the MIT CLI has no organization-license boundary.
honest_blockers: A pull_request run can prove the new org-owned CLI path; actual merge_group behavior remains structurally covered until a PR is admitted to the native merge queue.

The upstream v8.30.1 tag is no longer reachable from current master after upstream release-history mishandling, but the exact official Linux archive is bound to GitHub's published digest and an independently recomputed SHA-256.
session_entry.rollback: Revert the workflow, focused contract test, and packet together. Rollback restores the proprietary wrapper and therefore reintroduces the organization-license dependency and merge_group rejection; do not claim queue readiness after rollback.
